title: PEB Overview: What Is a Pre-Engineered Building?
description: Learn what a pre-engineered building is, how it is made and where it is used in Pakistan. A plain guide from Steel Mind Engineers.
h1: PEB Overview: What Is a Pre-Engineered Building?
quickAnswer: A pre-engineered building is a steel building made from parts that are designed and cut in a factory and then bolted together on your site. This removes most of the guesswork and much of the time from site work.
alt: Diagram of the main parts of a pre-engineered steel building.

faq.q: Is a PEB strong enough for Pakistani weather?
faq.a: Each PEB is designed for the wind, rain and load needs of its location. Share your site location so the engineer can set the design loads.

faq.q: How long does a PEB last?
faq.a: With a correct coating and regular maintenance, a steel building serves for decades.

blocks.text: A pre-engineered building is a steel building made from parts that are designed and cut in a factory. The parts are then bolted together on your site. Because the design is done in advance, there is little guesswork on site, and the building is ready for use sooner.

A PEB has five main groups of parts. The primary frame carries the main loads. The secondary members, called purlins and girts, carry the roof and wall sheets. The sheeting forms the roof and walls. The bracing keeps the building stable in wind. The accessories include doors, vents and skylights.

You give the use, size, location and load needs. Engineers design the frames and prepare drawings. The factory cuts, welds, paints and packs the parts. Trucks deliver the parts to your site. Crews bolt the parts together and fit the sheets. Foundation work on site runs at the same time as the factory work, and this overlap saves weeks.

PEBs suit factories, warehouses, dairy and poultry farms, workshops, showrooms, sports halls, cold stores, hangars and crane buildings. They work well wherever you need a large open floor with few columns.

Steel Mind offers the full PEB service: design, detailing, fabrication, painting, delivery and erection. The largest PEB projects include a 96,600 square foot crane shed and a 97,888 square foot crane and mezzanine shed for Haier at Raiwind.
